# INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED ENTEROCOCCUS INFECTION
Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Catheter removal is preferred but not required. Treatment is much more likely to be successful with removal of catheter. The decision about whether to remove the catheter depends on severity of illness, presence of resistant organisms, the need for the catheter, and how difficult catheter replacement would be.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.
[Approach to Endocarditis](endocarditis-approach-to)

# 

---

References:

- Mandell chapter: Infections Caused by Percutaneous Intravascular Devices
- Mermel et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases 49 (2009)
- Up-to-date article: Intravascular catheter-related infection: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, and microbiology
- Up-to-date article: Intravascular non-hemodialysis catheter-related infection: Treatment
Therapy:
## Inpatient

Treatment of susceptible E. Faecalis (Van A/B negative)

Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R <AND> ampicillin antibiotic lock therapy

Treatment of susceptible E. Faecium (Van A/B negative)

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R <AND> vancomycin antibiotic lock therapy

Treatment of resistant enterococcus (Van A/B positive)

### Treatment if the catheter is removed (preferred)
Refer to enterococcus bacteremia recommendations for antimicrobial selection
[Enterococci bacteremia](enterococci)

Duration of therapy:
For ampicillin or vancomycin susceptible isolates, treat for 7-14 days. A longer duration is required for resistant isolates. Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

### Treatment if catheter removal is not possible (less desirable)
Treatment of susceptible enterococcus (Van A/B negative on BCID Biofire)
Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] <AND> vancomycin antibiotic lock therapy Treatment of resistant enterococcus (Van A/B positive on BCID Biofire)
Linezolid 600 mg IV q12h ($$$$) [DI]

Duration of therapy:
For ampicillin or vancomycin susceptible isolates, treat concurrently with systemic and antibiotic lock therapy for 14 days. Consult Infectious Diseases for ampicillin and vancomycin resistant isolates.

*Local guidance (Omaha CDSS, Inpatient):*
systemic and antibiotic lock therapy for 14 days.
